chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Faddal and Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to Abu (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'Do you have a wife?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'I do not desire this world and what is in it, but I spent a night without having a wife.' Then he said, 'The two rak'ahs prayed by a married man are better than a single man who stands in prayer all night and fasts all day.'
Then Abu gave him seven dinars and said to him, 'Marry with these.'
Then Abu (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Take wives, for they provide sustenance for you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of marriage compared to celibacy in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the spiritual status of marriage by asserting that the two rak'ahs of a married man surpass the night prayer and daytime fasting of a celibate, highlighting that marital duties do not detract from worship but enhance it. He practically demonstrated this by giving a man seven dinars to marry, citing the Prophet’s saying that wives are a source of sustenance (rizq), which Shia scholars interpret as both material provision and spiritual tranquility. This narration underscores the Sunni-Shia consensus on the merit of marriage while emphasizing the Imam's role in guiding the community toward balanced religious practice.
